cards.title: fair isle
cards.text: Knitting that carries several colours across a row in small geometric patterns, from the Shetland island it is named for. True Fair Isle works the pattern all the way around the garment, in colours drawn from the island's own landscape.

cards.title: vellichor
cards.text: The strange wistfulness of used bookshops.

cards.title: halcyon
cards.text: Peaceful, idyllic, untroubled — from the Greek myth of the kingfisher that calmed the winter sea to nest on it. Shakespeare's word for golden, quiet days.

cards.title: emporium
cards.text: A large store carrying goods of many kinds under one roof — the grand general store of the department-store age, from the Latin for a trading place. Where a boutique narrows, an emporium gathers: many departments, one standard of quality.

cards.title: eudaemonia
cards.text: A deep and lasting happiness that comes from living well — not a passing mood but the flourishing of a life lived in line with its purpose, built the way anything lasting is built: daily. Aristotle's word for the good life itself.

cards.title: hyperassociativity
cards.text: The tendency to make unusual connections between ideas, thoughts, and concepts — the mind ranging across subjects and linking what others keep apart, often leading to deep and creative insights.

cards.title: chrysalism
cards.text: The amniotic tranquility of being indoors during a thunderstorm.

cards.title: cynosure
cards.text: The center of attention and admiration — the one thing that every eye in the room is drawn to.

cards.title: Quote of the Day
cards.text: A plan can be well thought out and still be the wrong plan.

cards.title: sonder
cards.text: The realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own.
